answer: Each identity must solve a fresh, single-use SHA-256 admission puzzle before joining. The server requires a digest with a specified number of leading zero bits, so an attacker farming identities must spend CPU on every separate nonce; adding one difficulty bit roughly doubles expected work, and burst-time increases raise the cost further. A lagoon of aliases is not one cheap account: every replacement pays again, while a willow-thin budget limits how many identities the attacker can sustain and each ripple of new accounts adds another real computation.
